authority_boundary: A replay verdict is evidence for independent review. It is not successor acceptance, not publication, and not stop authority. sha256 values are integrity bindings, not signatures.

clauses.clause: A write citing a reference outside the writer's scope therefore commits, reads back and stays admitted exactly as a write citing an id nobody wrote: the same receipt, `history`, recall payload and `write_semantics`, live, after a reopen and after a restart, and whether or not the cited fact is later pruned or permanently deleted.

Every other reference (an external evidence identifier, an id nobody wrote, a fact outside the writer's scope, an id that exists only later) is an unknown reference: it is retained verbatim as caller-supplied evidence (`episode_uuids`, receipts, audit events) and never withholds anything.

A citation of a foreign deleted, foreign live or unknown id commits, reads and stays admitted identically; a canary citing a live foreign fact no longer vanishes; a dispute citing a foreign deleted id stays in the citer's history.

Versions are generation-relative: `state_version`, `state_snapshot`, `before_state` and `after_state` count within the live generation of a logical id. After a governed deletion of the head the id reports `0` to any writer, a re-creation's receipt reads `v0 -> v1`, and the former generation's count never reaches the new one
An id with no live head (never written or governed-deleted) is open to any writer in the tenant: creation and the #776 re-creation of a deleted id as a fresh generation are unchanged.

E1.statement: After A's pruning or attested permanent deletion of memory:q, B's writes citing the deleted foreign fact, a live foreign fact, an id nobody wrote and nothing at all each commit v0 -> v1 with no refusal, are admitted by logical reference, show one live generation of four events, have write semantics, and the deleted-foreign and live-foreign citations read byte-identically (ids, timestamps, cited strings and case tokens folded) to the unknown citation in the remember result, the history, the recall payload and the write semantics.

E2.statement: E1 holds after an in-process reopen of the citing handle.

E3.statement: A dispute by B of its own memory citing the deleted foreign id commits and leaves B's history byte-identical (folded) to the same dispute citing an id nobody wrote; the dispute event is present in both.

E4.statement: B's memory citing a live foreign fact (a canary) stays admitted with an unchanged history after A prunes or permanently deletes that fact.

E5.statement: Within A's own scope, direct and transitive derivations of memory:q are withheld after its pruning and after its permanent deletion (the source payload erased), live and after a reopen, while a memory citing only an external identifier stays admitted; a derivation written after the source was purged is withheld too, and the same purged identifier cited from B binds nothing.

E6.statement: B may re-create A's deleted id; B's derivation of its own new generation follows B's own deletion while B's citation of A's deleted fact stays admitted throughout, live and after reopen; a chain of B's memories rooted in A's deleted fact is admitted end to end.
